content: Hello! how can I help today?
I’m self-employed and made $200K last year. What can I still contribute for retirement?
You can contribute up to **20% of net self-employment income**, capped at **$69,000 for 2024**, into a SEP IRA—even if you're filing near the **extended deadline**.
How do I calculate net SE income?
Take your **Schedule C net profit**, subtract **½ SE tax**, then apply 20%. Most use **IRS Pub. 560** or a tax tool to get this precisely.
**Yes**—use **Form 5305-SEP** to establish the plan, and report your contribution on **Schedule 1**, Line 16. This directly lowers your AGI and boosts eligibility for other tax benefits.
